q: The Luzin-Suslin theorem characterises Borel subsets among analytic sets. It states that an analytic subset A of a Polish space is Borel if and only if:
opts: The complement X\A is also analytic (A is both Σ¹₁ and Π¹₁ — bianalytic)
exp: Luzin-Suslin (or Suslin's theorem): a subset of a Polish space is Borel iff it is both analytic (Σ¹₁) and co-analytic (Π¹₁). If A is analytic and its complement is also analytic, then A is Borel. This is a non-trivial separation theorem—there exist analytic sets that are not Borel.
